text:
Detailed Faculty Review: AHBn (Dr. Abdul Halim Bhuiyan)
Course: MAT125
Semester: Summer 2025
Grade attained: A-
Disclaimer: Faculty reviews are entirely subjective, so take every review with a grain of salt.
Personality & Behavior: AHBn is one of the most calm and collected faculties I've come across. He is soft-spoken at all times, never raises his voice, never behaves rudely, and is very approachable. Literally the definition of a "chill guy".
Teaching: He delivers most of his lecture in English and only switches to Bangla when he needs to clarify something. However, I found him to be average, or even below average, at teaching, as I would find myself lost during most of his lectures, despite coming to a realization that most of the topics discussed were quite easy later on. Him using 3 books simultaneously to teach until the mid didn't help either.
Note-taking during his classes is a challenge on its own, as he almost never writes down any math properly on the board. Plus he has this habit of writing on random positions on the board, making things even more confusing. In the end, I had to rely on self-studying to learn the concepts properly.
Coursework & Grading: The best part about his course is that his exams, especially his quizzes, are relatively very easy. He sometimes takes quizzes on single chapters or even just a single topic. He took 4 quizzes in total in my section. The mid and final are of moderate difficulty, but he clearly states what type of questions to expect during the review classes, which makes the preparation a bit easier.
However, he has a very peculiar style of giving assignments. At the end of each chapter, he chooses a bunch of random questions from the chapter exercises in class and tells us to do them. After a bunch of chapters are finished, he then collects the assignments together. So, if you miss any of the classes, you're gonna have to collect that day's given tasks from one of your classmates. He doesn't post the exercise numbers on Canvas. He doesn't post quiz announcements on Canvas either.
In terms of marking our scripts, he's very fair and gives partial marks for incorrect answers. He does curve, but does so only with our assignment, quiz, and attendance marks. He curved and updated our marksheets right in front of us during the last class. He outright told us that he wouldn't be curving our mid and final marks. I estimate I got 29 or 28 (out of 35) at worst on my final when I needed 30 to get an A, but he didn't curve it as he said. This does feel a bit demoralizing when you performed exceptionally throughout the semester, but I suppose fair is fair.
TL;DR: He's friendly but doesn't teach well. You can do well on his exams fairly easily, but if you slip up even a bit on your mid or final, your grade will get cooked. Overall, wouldn't recommend him for the average student.

Faculty Review: AHBn (Dr. Abdul Halim Bhuiyan) 
Course: MAT125 
he's a new faculty member, so there aren't many reviews about him yet. i asked a few of my coursemates, and this post is based on our shared experience.
Teaching: 
he teaches in English and speaks slowly, but if you pay close attention, you'll be able to understand him. it's super important to take proper notes during his lectures, you really need to note down every single thing he says. if you genuinely try to understand the math in class and revise your notes before the exam, getting a good / decent grade should be easy. he also pays attention to each student individually.
Quizzes & Assignments:
he conducts 4(or 5) quizzes (we had only 3 because the 4th got canceled due to rain, he's very considerate that way). he counted the best 2. the number of quizzes and how they’re counted may adjust depending on the class’s overall performance, ensuring everyone has the best chance to do well. the questions are directly based on class notes, maybe just with slightly larger matrices sometimes, but they're totally doable if your concepts are clear. he takes 2 assignments (also based on class notes) and counts their average. 
Mid & Final: 
again, taking proper notes and reviewing them is the key. same as quizzes. 
in our case, he gave almost everything from the exercises he suggested from the books, so make sure to practice those well. also does partial marking. 
i missed two of his classes before finals and struggled a bit because i had missed some key topics. thankfully, his revision class helped me catch up. 
he is a very good human being, treated me and my friend like his younger sisters and would troll us in a fun, lighthearted way. he might seem strict at first glance, but he's actually really chill and approachable. See less
